title: OpenAI ChatCompletions contractual mapper — streaming window & idempotency reconciliation
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Customers using the OpenAI Chat Completions (OA-CC) compatibility surface expect two semantics that diverge from Redwood's native runtime: (1) a framed streaming window and event model (partial deltas + stream end) with different backpressure characteristics, and (2) an idempotency/contract layer for tool/function calling where OA-CC uses a single function_call object and Redwood uses eventized tool invocation + callback pattern.

Goal: Implement a thin compatibility mapper that translates OA-CC request/response semantics to Redwood native RPCs without regressing streaming latency or introducing duplicate tool invocations. The mapper should: preserve partial tokens/events for streaming consumers, synthesize idempotency markers so function calls are invoked exactly-once (subject to Redwood guarantees), and emit telemetry for mismatches so we can refine kernel/batching behavior.

Scope: This ticket focuses on the request/response mapping module and its streaming reconciliation logic. It does NOT include full console UX changes for visibility (follow-up ticket planned), nor Dedicated capacity autoscaling integration (separate work).
acceptance_criteria: OA-CC style streaming responses are produced over our streaming wire protocol with the same sequence of partial text & role/meta events for 90% of test prompts in the compatibility suite (see linked tests).

Tool/function calls initiated by OA-CC function_call semantics result in at-most-once invocation of Redwood tool RPCs for idempotent tools and exactly-once semantics for tools with external idempotency tokens (documented behavior).
Backpressure/flow-control: large prompt + generation workloads do not cause token amplification or unbounded memory growth in the mapper (CI stress tests pass with <200ms median extra latency).
Telemetry events emitted for: mapping errors, truncated tool payloads, and stream window boundary misalignments (events visible in staging console dashboard).
Compatibility mapper code has unit and integration coverage and a non-flaky e2e test that runs in CI against local runtime shim (green in main).
implementation_notes: High-level approach: implement a stateless translator that accepts OA-CC HTTP payloads (both single-request and chunked), normalizes role/message/stop tokens, and forwards to Redwood generation RPCs. For streaming, reconcile OA-CC partial frames to Redwood token deltas by maintaining a small sliding window of last N KV-cache checkpoints (N=3 default).

Idempotency strategy: generate an internal idempotency key derived from OA-CC request.id + client-supplied idempotency_key header when present. If none provided, synthesize a weak key but treat tool calls as potentially retriable (emit warning telemetry).

Tool/function mapping: map OA-CC function_call.name to Redwood tool identifiers. For function args, validate JSON schema; if validation fails, return a structured error object that adheres to OA-CC error shape so downstream clients can recover without breaking streaming consumers.

Backpressure: honor Redwood runtime token emit pacing. When OA-CC client is slow-consuming, pause token production by buffering up to 4 chunks and then apply soft-dropback policy (emit a "content_truncated" metadata event).

Streaming semantics: on receiving a stream chunk from runtime, produce OA-CC compatible chunk frames: 'delta' objects for partial text and a final 'done' event that includes function_call if invoked. Ensure chunk ordering and sequence numbers are monotonically increasing even across reconnects.
rollout_plan: 2) Integration tests in staging with synthetic OA-CC clients (canary traffic).
3) Enable compatibility mapper by default for new OA-CC users in staging; opt-in for existing customers.
4) Monitor telemetry for 72 hours, roll back if tool call duplicate rate > 0.1% or stream mismatches exceed threshold.
5) Gradual rollout to production in 3 phases across regions (us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1).
tests: Unit: mapping table coverage for 100+ OA-CC edge message shapes (invalid json, nested function args, zero-length messages).
Integration: streaming window reconciliation harness that replays large generation traces and verifies OA-CC frame sequence identical to gold output except for permissible metadata differences.
E2E: deploy mapper behind an internal OA-CC compat host and run the OA-CC conformance suite (tests in ci/compat).
Load: 50k requests/hour with 1-2% requiring tool calls; verify no more than 0.05% duplicate tool invocations.
